sections.title: Sexual violence: examination and evidence (MoHFW 2014)
sections.alert: MoHFW 2014: never do a per-vaginal (two-finger) test to establish sexual violence; a per-vaginal examination is done only in an adult woman when medically indicated. The size of the vaginal introitus and the state of the hymen have no bearing on sexual violence, so document only findings relevant to this assault, such as fresh tears, bleeding or oedema. Do not record past sexual conduct or give any opinion on habituation to sexual intercourse. First aid and treatment are free and must not wait for a police requisition or FIR: inform the police, and give full care even if the survivor does not wish to take part in the investigation.

sections.title: Red flags
sections.alert: Treat first: first aid and life-saving treatment need no consent and must not wait for the police or paperwork. Child under 18: inform the police; a woman doctor examines a girl, with a parent or a person the child trusts present; when the child needs care and protection, involve the Child Welfare Committee through the police, and inform the Committee if a parent or guardian is acting against the child's interest. Poisoning: follow the acute poisoning protocol and preserve samples. Possible self-harm: follow the self-harm and suicide risk protocol. Death with injury, poisoning or an unclear cause: inform the police and the Registrar; the cause of death is certified through the police and post-mortem process, and a manner not yet known is shown as Pending investigation.

advice.title: Care after sexual violence
advice.text: What happened is not your fault. Your treatment here is free, and you will be cared for whether or not you take part in a police case. Take all the medicines given to you for the full course, and come back for the follow-up tests on the dates written here. You can ask for counselling support at any time.

advice.title: Your examination report
advice.text: You have a right to a free copy of your medical examination report. Keep it safely with your other papers, and bring it to your follow-up visits.

advice.title: Cause of death certificate (for the family)
advice.text: The doctor gives the medical certificate of cause of death to the Registrar with the death report, and a copy to the nearest relative. The cause of death is kept confidential and is not shown on the death certificate issued by the Registrar.
